title: improv·artist · fluid (Helen Frankenthaler)
mutation_directive: improv artist: fluid via Helen Frankenthaler

improv_extras.practice: soak-stain; thinned pigment soaks the canvas; geological flow

v1.feedback: The Frankenthaler concept genuinely drives the design — differential growth as soak-stain is a smart reframing, and the three translucent overlapping pools on raw-linen background read immediately. Two things to sharpen: the triangle-fan fill from centroid makes each stain look like a flat geometric pie rather than the uneven pigment-density gradients of real soak-stain — consider a radial noise term in the fragment shader that modulates alpha based on distance-from-centroid with irregular falloff, so pigment pools unevenly like actual watercolor. Second, with MAX_VERTS at 1200 split across three layers, the boundary complexity plateaus early and the forms can feel inert after warmup — either raise the cap or add a second slower growth pass that occasionally spawns new seed rings where stains overlap, reinforcing the geological-layering aspect of the brief.

v2.feedback: The differential-growth stain pools genuinely map Frankenthaler's soak-stain process — pigment pooling, granulation, and irregular radial spread all read as watercolor-on-linen within 2 seconds, and the palette (rose, cerulean, ochre) is restrained and period-appropriate. The top-down camera looking at a flat canvas plane is the right framing for this concept but the forms stay small relative to the 50-unit canvas — push initial radii and maxV higher so the stains bleed toward canvas edges and overlap, which is where Frankenthaler's geological flow actually happens. Add subtle inter-pool color bleeding at overlap zones (blend fragment alphas with neighbor hue) to sell the soaking-into-raw-canvas effect rather than three isolated puddles sitting on top of linen.
